title: Man died of drug overdose while in police custody: Watchdog
subtitle: A London police officer could have taken an overdosing prisoner to the hospital sooner, but the officer's failure to do so didn't result in the man's death, Ontario's police watchdog has ruled.
article: A London police officer could have taken an overdosing prisoner to the hospital sooner, but the officer's failure to do so didn't result in the man's death, Ontario's police watchdog has ruled.
The Special Investigations Unit (SIU) on Thursday cleared the London police officer, whose name wasn't released, of any wrongdoing in the Feb. 1 custody death of Fabian Hart.
Police responding to a reported domestic disturbance arrested Hart, 34, around 3:30 p.m. for violating a court and placed him in a cell at police headquarters, the SIU said.

The next day, Hart began to shake and his condition deteriorated, purportedly the result of alcohol withdrawal, and an officer arranged to have him sent to the hospital shortly after 9 a.m., the SIU said.

But before he was taken to the hospital, Hart needed immediate medical attention, so officers administered live-saving measures before paramedics arrived and took him to the hospital, where he died shortly before 10 a.m. His cause of death was a methamphetamine overdose, the SIU said.
Medical experts ruled Hart took methamphetamine minutes before he went into seizures, the SIU said.

Video examined by SIU investigators showed Hart talking with a sergeant at 4:05 p.m. while being processed at police headquarters, saying he'd taken three vodka shots that day but hadn't done any drugs, the SIU said.

Hart's condition started to deteriorate the next day around 1:40 a.m. and he told an officer that he was going into alcohol withdrawal and needed a sugary snack, which he was provided, and officers monitored Hart throughout the night.

The officer at the centre of the watchdog's investigation performed chest compressions on Hart around 8:40 a.m. before another officer administered Narcan, the drug used to reverse opioid overdoses, and then used a defibrillator on Hart, who no longer had a pulse, the SIU said.

The subject officer declined to be interviewed by SIU investigators or turn over their notes, as is an officer's legal right, the watchdog said. SIU director Joseph Martino said the subject officer's liability may have been different had he known that Hart likely had methamphetamine on him.

"The complainant, however, had denied consuming any drugs as he was being booked prior to being lodged in cells. Nor is there any suggestion that the custodial staff, including the (subject officer), was derelict in allowing the complainant to retrieve and consume drugs while in cells," Martino wrote in his report.

"This, together with the medical evidence indicating the methamphetamines were very likely absorbed by the complainant's system within minutes of his medical episode, raises the possibility that the drugs were secreted inside the complainant's body while he was in custody."
The SIU investigates all cases of gunfire, serious injury, death and allegations of sexual assault involving police.
Geralt Hart, Fabian's father, told The Free Press the family has many questions left unanswered but declined to comment further at this time.
